newsitem.title: UK: CLM Insurance to continue acquistion plans.
newsitem.headline: CLM Insurance to continue acquistion plans.

text.p: CLM Insurance said on Friday it would continue its strategy of acquiring a managing agency and developing managed syndicates to complement its existing spread of Lloyd's syndicate participations.

CLM said it was disappointed that Benfield & Rea Investment Trust (BRIT) had been successful in its rival bid for HCG Lloyds Investment Trust. It said it had been actively in discussions with HCG about revising the terms of its own offer but this would now lapse.
Earlier HCG recommended its shareholders to accept BRIT's offer, which was declared unconditional by BRIT on Thursday.

"HCG shareholders who do not want to receive BRIT shares should consider selling their HCG shares in the market provided the price attainable (net of expenses) is in excess of the cash alternative of 117 pence being offered by BRIT," HCG said in a statement.

It said the BRIT board had waived the condition of the offer relating to the acquisition of a minority interest in Wren Holdings Group Plc but the offer remained conditional on Lloyd's regulatory consent and BRIT shareholder approval.
CLM said that despite losing in the battle for HCG, it believes "there are exciting opportunities for investors arising at Lloyd's following the implemtation of reconstruction and renewal".

"CLM shareholders can look forward to receiving in 1997 the first of a stream of substantial dividends as underwriting profits for the 1994 and subsequent year of account come available for distribution," it added.
